Matheus, the AgentSpec author who runs scripts/rollout-agentspec.sh to vendor AgentSpec updates into all 11 downstream repos, and the maintainers of those 11 repos who must review each incoming rollout before merging it, currently have no way to preview which files a rollout will create, overwrite, or skip before the script actually writes to disk, so they either run it blind against a real repo or read the script source line by line to guess its plan; add a --dry-run flag to scripts/rollout-agentspec.sh that, when passed, computes and prints the full file copy plan (source path, destination path, and create/overwrite/skip action for every file under .claude/, plugin/, and docs/) to stdout and exits 0 without creating, deleting, or modifying a single file on disk; success is measured by 2 new pytest cases added under tests/ covering --dry-run -- one run against an empty target directory with no existing .claude/ tree, and one run against a populated target directory containing files that would be overwritten -- both asserting zero filesystem writes via before/after mtime comparison and an exit code of 0, plus 100% of the existing rollout-agentspec.sh test suite continuing to pass unmodified; running the script without --dry-run must remain byte-for-byte identical to its current behavior, with no new required arguments and no change to the default copy plan; explicitly out of scope for this change are any changes to the existing --verbose flag, support for remote SSH/scp rollout targets, and any change to the dry-run output's exact text formatting beyond the three required fields (source path, destination path, action).
